topics.name: Spatiotemporal visual modeling
topics.summary: Pose and camera cues, geometric tracking, motion transfer, and video-language benchmarks recur across these sequence models. The papers cover animation, temporal localization, identity preservation, world-model assessment, and interactive video generation, with emphasis on structure and continuity.

topics.name: Spectral and multimodal imaging
topics.summary: Spectral bands, sparse observations, and structured priors support reconstruction, classification, enhancement, and scientific inference. The studies span hyperspectral and EEG signals, super-resolution, Gaussian geometry, and physics-based fields, emphasizing cross-sensor robustness and fine-detail recovery.

topics.name: Reinforcement learning for reasoning and control
topics.summary: These studies improve sequential policies through credit assignment, external rollouts, self-play, rubric rewards, value learning, and constrained exploration. Applications range from language reasoning and code generation to manipulation and navigation, with recurring concerns about stability, transfer, and useful feedback.

topics.name: Information retrieval and evidence-grounded agents
topics.summary: Document graphs, knowledge graphs, structured repositories, and persistent evidence states support multi-hop retrieval and agent search. Evaluations focus on coverage, provenance, stopping, failure diagnosis, and context effects in question answering, code, research, and long-horizon workflows.

topics.name: Efficient neural inference and compression
topics.summary: The papers reduce serving or storage cost with token compression, cache quantization, sparse attention, semantic caching, lower-precision arithmetic, and parallel refinement. They measure task quality alongside latency, memory, energy, and acceptance so efficiency gains remain tied to useful predictions.

topics.name: Safety, alignment, and robustness of language models
topics.summary: Safety is examined through agent benchmarks, educational deployment, multi-turn pressure, enterprise policy, chemistry audits, and repository governance. The common concern is whether surface compliance, confidence, or aggregate success remains reliable under adversarial, contextual, or high-stakes conditions.

topics.name: Bayesian decision and question answering
topics.summary: Bayesian updating, posterior calibration, evidence weighting, and uncertainty-aware answer selection appear across visual QA, tabular generation, compliance, intervention analysis, and multimodal retrieval. Exact or probabilistic checks separate plausible answers from decisions supported by available evidence.

topics.name: Autonomous driving perception and safety
topics.summary: Driving systems combine cameras, radar, bird's-eye-view representations, weather synthesis and restoration, world models, and language-guided reasoning. Results target collision avoidance, compact edge inference, faithful trajectory supervision, and robustness to rain, fog, attacks, and changing scenes.

topics.name: Vision-language grounding and reasoning
topics.summary: These papers study links between visual content, language, and action across spatial queries, document extraction, web relevance, urban inspection, medical imaging, and robot policies. They favor geometric supervision, calibrated confidence, candidate scoring, and targeted intervention over unconstrained generation.

topics.name: Geometric optimization and registration
topics.summary: Geometric optimization supplies smooth trajectories, registrations, tensor decompositions, obstacle avoidance, and parameterized models. Across mathematical analyses and clinical or robotic measurements, the recurring goal is preserving structure while controlling curvature, conditioning, nonsmoothness, and alignment error.

topics.name: Robotic manipulation and humanoid control
topics.summary: Embodied systems combine visual perception, task execution, teleoperation, contact control, and state-aware action policies. Experiments span construction, aerial surface interaction, humanoid operation, search and rescue, and safety certification, emphasizing smooth behavior under physical constraints.

topics.name: Bias and fairness in AI systems
topics.summary: The studies analyze demographic, linguistic, social, and programmatic bias in language, vision, and generative systems. They use controlled prompts, behavioral audits, causal decompositions, and population-aware criteria to distinguish representation gaps from output decisions and aggregate performance.

topics.name: 3D reconstruction and neural rendering
topics.summary: Gaussian primitives, feed-forward SLAM, generative priors, and view synthesis are used to recover geometry from sparse or moving observations. The papers target efficient rendering, editable scenes, large-baseline synthesis, and stable representations for robotics, simulation, and teleoperation.

topics.name: Policy distillation and continual post-training
topics.summary: Teacher traces, privileged signals, consistency objectives, and capability-preserving regularization guide policy improvement after initial training. The applications span reasoning, agentic reinforcement learning, enterprise workflows, and diffusion language models, balancing specialization with retention and deployment cost.

topics.name: Time-series forecasting and monitoring
topics.summary: Forecasting and monitoring methods model latent regimes, direction, changepoints, degradation, telemetry, climate variability, and operational demand. The evaluations prioritize finite-sample attribution, calibrated decisions, event timing, and useful explanations rather than relying on a single aggregate error.

topics.name: Adaptive routing and uncertainty-aware computation
topics.summary: Learned routers allocate resolution, expert capacity, evidence, or model choice according to uncertainty and task difficulty. Across diffusion models, multimodal perception, medical analysis, and control, the studies seek lower cost while preserving difficult cases and providing interpretable risk signals.

topics.name: Recommendation and multimodal retrieval
topics.summary: Matching markets, knowledge graphs, hypergraphs, sparse-dense embeddings, and modality completion support personalized recommendation and search. The recurring objectives are relevance, coverage, explainability, robustness to missing inputs, and efficient ranking under changing user or item distributions.

topics.name: Diffusion and generative modeling
topics.summary: Diffusion and transport formulations are applied to motion, medical analysis, Earth observation, language, and image generation. The papers investigate one-step mappings, stochastic optimization, latent representations, sampling guarantees, and quality-preserving acceleration across data types.

topics.name: Federated and distributed learning
topics.summary: Federated methods address heterogeneous clients, privacy-aware participation, medical records, climate and flood observations, and distributed event modeling. Their designs personalize aggregation or feature exchange while limiting harmful transfer, communication overhead, and sensitivity to uneven data quality.

topics.name: Agent memory and personalization
topics.summary: Persona graphs, co-evolving retrieval, dual-track facts, and editable memory banks help agents preserve useful information over long interactions. The studies connect storage policy, evidence, usage, revision, and failure recovery to more reliable personalization and continual adaptation.

topics.name: Recurrent attention and long-context modeling
topics.summary: Recurrent state, retention mechanisms, hierarchical indexing, context distillation, and cross-layer memory reduce the cost of extended sequences. Results examine what information survives compression, how retrieval changes with iteration, and when compact state can replace full attention.

topics.name: Digital twins and scientific sensing
topics.summary: Digital-twin studies combine learned operators, anomaly detection, thermography, EEG analysis, heritage imaging, and multimodal scene representations. The methods use physical geometry, material properties, or sensor-specific structure to improve monitoring and simulation of real environments.

topics.name: Remote sensing segmentation and visual sensing
topics.summary: Overhead and field imagery is processed with click propagation, active sampling, frequency cues, foundation-model features, and change captioning. Applications include crop surveys, solar defects, disaster mapping, rip currents, and environmental monitoring, with emphasis on sparse labels and fine structures.

topics.name: Tool-using language agents
topics.summary: Executable tools, graph analysis, software environments, databases, and technical artifacts are used to test agent planning and recovery. The papers evaluate harnesses, audits, repair loops, authorization, and interactive debugging, showing that reliable execution requires state and verification beyond fluent output.

topics.name: Structured classification and prediction
topics.summary: Classification systems handle audio sources, document content, segmentation, multiple-choice answers, and physiological or behavioral labels. The work compares training-free and learned approaches, studies fine-grained errors, and uses selective or structured outputs to improve robustness and interpretability.

topics.name: Reflective editing and system repair
topics.summary: Visual editing, model repair, hardware debugging, and interactive agent improvement rely on localized diagnosis followed by constrained changes. Across images, repositories, neural modules, and conversational systems, the studies separate useful intervention from cosmetic modification and measure preservation of valid behavior.

topics.name: Optimization and learning theory
topics.summary: Theoretical and algorithmic analyses study curvature, gradient flow, sparse optimization, parameter perturbation, operator learning, and stochastic search. Results connect conditioning, geometry, regularization, and approximation error to convergence behavior and the reliability of learned solutions.

topics.name: Feature selection and inference latency
topics.summary: Feature and model selection methods allocate computation according to information value, uncertainty, or deployment limits. Applications include time-series classification, anomaly detection, robot action prediction, point-cloud adaptation, neural pruning, and welfare-aware selection across heterogeneous groups.

topics.name: Memory authorization and privacy controls
topics.summary: Persistent memories, semantic caches, authorization tokens, scope-bound disclosure, and cryptographic mutation controls are treated as security-sensitive state. The papers address replay, stale authority, private communication, and concurrent edits, emphasizing protections that survive retries and later retrieval.

topics.name: Finite-sample statistical inference
topics.summary: These studies derive nonasymptotic guarantees for distributional drift, phase retrieval, logistic and ridge regression, mean estimation, Langevin sampling, and sparse least squares. They expose conditioning, observability, dependence, and approximation assumptions that determine whether uncertainty statements are informative.

topics.name: Semantic representations and model analysis
topics.summary: Representation studies compare conceptual geometry, semantic alignment, topological structure, formula understanding, and black-box behavior across model layers and languages. They use probing, graph or topological summaries, and intervention to relate internal organization to transfer, ambiguity, and explanation quality.

topics.name: Medical AI and biomedical imaging
topics.summary: Clinical systems integrate imaging, patient graphs, anatomy-aware routing, medical foundation models, and multimodal diagnosis. Evaluations cover lesion analysis, chest and brain imaging, patient classification, and physiological prediction, with attention to calibration, transfer, and clinically meaningful failure modes.

topics.name: Deepfake and expression analysis
topics.summary: Forgery detection and human-expression modeling use multimodal embeddings, demographic cues, facial dynamics, open-set recognition, and cellular-scale representations. The studies emphasize generalization beyond known artifacts, identity preservation, and the distinction between visual realism and trustworthy provenance.

topics.name: Image restoration and visual enhancement
topics.summary: Restoration methods address darkness, motion blur, weather, scratches, thermal detail, and high-resolution video degradation. They combine recurrent or semantic priors with generative and low-level reconstruction models, evaluating both perceptual quality and preservation of geometry or temporal continuity.

topics.name: Open-set recognition and re-identification
topics.summary: Recognition under changing viewpoint, season, species, and domain uses calibrated similarity, clustering, canonical geometry, and selective prediction. The applications span aerial-ground person matching, wildlife annotation, animal re-identification, and evolving visual populations where closed-set assumptions are unreliable.

topics.name: Domain adaptation and graph-based detection
topics.summary: Adaptation methods handle data drift, point-cloud mismatch, graph structure, vulnerability paths, and misinformation signals. They combine lightweight transfer, graph reasoning, formal checks, and domain-specific evidence to improve robustness when deployment conditions differ from training assumptions.

topics.name: Speech and audio processing
topics.summary: Speech and audio studies cover dysarthric recognition, translation, expressive generation, psychoacoustic enhancement, and language-model readout. Datasets and probing analyses emphasize speaker, scene, disfluency, dialect, and acoustic variation rather than treating speech as clean text alone.

topics.name: Dynamical systems and spatiotemporal learning
topics.summary: These papers learn or analyze evolving systems through Lie symmetries, dynamic games, climate and physical fields, distributed control, and finite-horizon interactions. The methods connect structural priors and temporal coupling to prediction, planning, and stability under changing observations.

topics.name: Model forgetting and representation scope
topics.summary: The work examines how models retain, discard, or expose information across layers, modalities, and task boundaries. Topics include weight perturbation, attention heads, unlearned knowledge, chart semantics, missing-data definitions, and representations whose apparent alignment does not guarantee usable meaning.

topics.name: Human-centered interaction and virtual reality
topics.summary: Interactive systems are evaluated through rehabilitation games, virtual agents, aging, water sensing, and trust in technology. The studies treat usability, autonomy, ambiguity, emotion, and material context as part of system performance rather than secondary presentation concerns.

topics.name: Geometric assembly and physics-informed modeling
topics.summary: Physical structure guides learning for interlocking assemblies, inverse scattering, electromagnetic behavior, and geometry-aware generation. The methods use constraints, recursive construction, energy or equation-based priors, and material structure to improve extrapolation beyond purely data-driven fits.

topics.name: Surgical vision and cognitive modeling
topics.summary: The papers connect perception, tissue affordances, attention, cognitive workload, and formal accounts of decision behavior. Surgical systems use motion and scene cues for anticipatory framing, while cognitive models represent memory and social context with explicit state or symbolic structure.

topics.name: Evaluation, ranking, and citation analysis
topics.summary: Assessment methods study automated scoring, search ranking, citation or indicator quality, and research-agent evidence. They compare human and model judgments, inspect criterion-level reliability, and seek measures that reflect coverage, usefulness, and factual support rather than stylistic fluency.

topics.name: Sequence labeling and robust recognition
topics.summary: Sequence models address temporal aggregation, tracking, action or sign recognition, causal reliability, and label ambiguity. The recurring techniques include stable representations, cross-window transfer, selective decisions, and explicit treatment of unreliable pose, sensor, or annotation evidence.

topics.name: Scientific representation and explainability
topics.summary: Scientific and engineering models are assessed through attribution stability, formula or diagram structure, explanatory summaries, and physically meaningful features. The papers ask whether explanations remain stable across data and users and whether symbolic or visual representations support discovery rather than only prediction.

topics.name: Benchmarking, rubrics, and relational analysis
topics.summary: Benchmark design and evaluation methods study rubric dependence, relational structure, correlation, and decision validity in model-generated answers. The work favors dependency-aware scoring, targeted criteria, and analyses that reveal when aggregate agreement hides redundancy or systematic failure.

topics.name: Wireless, power, and wearable systems
topics.summary: Signal-processing and hardware studies cover radar, conductive textiles, transient magnetization, wearable power transfer, and neural or embedded sensing. Their methods combine compact learned models with physical channel or circuit constraints to improve detection, efficiency, and deployment resilience.

topics.name: Human behavior and decision support
topics.summary: These studies model social decisions, human-AI behavior, conformity, and interaction outcomes using simulations, surveys, and longitudinal measurement. They examine how trust, pressure, feedback, and group dynamics alter decisions and whether system metrics capture those effects.

topics.name: Software agents and language technology
topics.summary: Language models support requirements interviews, photonic or hardware code generation, repository workflows, multilingual writing, and conversational editing. These systems combine scripts, retrieval, structured traces, and user feedback to manage domain constraints and improve practical collaboration.

topics.name: Structured retrieval and dataset construction
topics.summary: The papers build or exploit structured indexes, layered representations, multimodal similarity, benchmark datasets, and missing-data models. Their common aim is making search and learning more reproducible by exposing fields, relations, temporal coverage, or annotation choices.

topics.name: Coordinates, world models, and scene descriptions
topics.summary: World-model research links spatial coordinates, learned descriptions, agent environments, and narrative reconstruction. The methods use geometric state, persistent scenes, and structured descriptions to support planning, simulation, or interactive experiences beyond static image generation.

topics.name: Evolutionary optimization and continual adaptation
topics.summary: Evolutionary and continual methods search over policies, strategies, operators, and workflows while reusing prior solutions. Applications include symbolic discovery, multi-agent control, hardware repair, and long-running adaptation, with emphasis on efficient exploration under changing objectives.

topics.name: Annotation, morphology, and mobility analysis
topics.summary: Annotation and recognition systems use morphology, seasonal priors, mobility or pose structure, and linguistic form to handle sparse or variable labels. The applications span astronomy, wildlife, ancient languages, and human activity, where domain knowledge improves transfer and interpretation.

topics.name: Clinical normalization and biomechanical sensing
topics.summary: These studies reconcile measurements across records, sensors, and physical tasks. Clinical medication conventions, robot dynamics, gait force estimation, and contact behavior show that timing, reference frames, and sensor placement can materially change inferred outcomes.

topics.name: Text, literature, and pilot studies
topics.summary: The papers develop text resources, literary or linguistic analyses, educational pilots, and biosignal applications. They combine corpus construction, human studies, and lightweight modeling to examine how language, training, and physiological signals behave in realistic settings.

topics.name: Decision-making and cognitive engineering
topics.summary: Formal decision models and engineering assistants address military simulation, moral reasoning, engine prediction, and explainable cognitive architectures. The studies combine structured states, domain rules, and learned estimates to make complex decisions more inspectable and operationally useful.

topics.name: Nonlinear models and parametric estimation
topics.summary: Nonlinear and parametric methods model pricing, terrain, array or point-cloud structure, and other systems where interactions are difficult to capture with simple linear features. The papers use compact architectures or structured parameters to improve efficiency and physical or geometric fidelity.

topics.name: Collective intelligence and embodied resilience
topics.summary: Collective and embodied systems study self-assembly, distributed construction, resilience, and socialized discovery under limited information or physical disturbance. Local signals, morphological diversity, and multi-scale coordination support robust behavior without requiring complete global state.
